_comment: Every word a patient reads. Edit wording here, not in code. Any edit changes this file's fingerprint and invalidates prior sign-off, so it must be re-reviewed (see governance/readiness.py).
urgent_help: Get help right away (call 911) for chest pain, fainting, trouble breathing, or severe confusion. If a child may have eaten a cannabis product, call 911 or Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 now.

oral_redose.text: We noticed a second dose by mouth soon after the first. Edibles, oils and capsules can take 2 hours or more to work, so taking more too soon can make you feel very unwell later. Please do not take any more today. Rest somewhere safe and do not drive. Your care team has been told.

adverse_effect.text: You logged {effects}. Thank you for writing it down. Please do not take your next dose until your care team contacts you. They have been told and will help you decide what to do next.

multiple_changes.text: It looks like more than one thing changed at once (for example the product, the amount or how you take it). Changing one thing at a time helps you and your care team see what is really helping.

missing_log_fields.text: A few details were missing from your recent log ({fields}). Writing them down before each dose takes a minute and helps your care team tailor your plan to you.

medication_check.text: One of your other medicines can interact with cannabis products. Your pharmacist and care team have been told and may adjust your plan. Please keep taking your medicines as prescribed unless they tell you otherwise.

review_questions: Is every statement clinically correct and consistent with your protocols?
Does any message tell a patient to do something they should not do without speaking to you?
Would a patient know exactly what to do next after reading it?
Is the tone kind and free of blame?
Is anything confusing, frightening or easy to misread?
Is the emergency guidance correct for your service area and patient population?
What language or accessibility versions are needed (e.g. Spanish, large print, screen reader)?
